name: The Grey household at 2010 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_grey_w_l

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2010 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr..

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2010, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The four live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: Jessie Grey (one of two unmarried daughters in 1900; which one is the 1904 "Miss Grey" is not known, so both are named in that line's note); Walter Grey (a grown son the 1904 Blue Book does not list at the house); Florence Grey (one of two unmarried daughters in 1900; named in the note on "Miss Grey"). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Miss Grey
persons.printed_as: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr.
persons.note: The Blue Book prints '& dr.' after the household's name: an unmarried daughter at home, not named. 'Miss Grey' is the book's own form of address, not a recorded name. The 1900 census lists the unmarried daughters at home as Jessie Grey (born May 1875, in Illinois, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 34, leaf n810); Florence Grey (born December 1880, in Illinois, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 36, leaf n810). Which of them the 1904 line stands for, the book does not say.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (waitress); born April 1878, in Ireland, came to the United States in 1894, single. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
